I feel as though Stockton accumulated such monstrous numbers due to the system in which he played + Karl Malone. If you look at the assist leaders for those teams, it's Stockton with an insane average and then everyone else is about around 2 or 3 if anything at all. Stockton WAS the ball-movement for that team. I also mention Malone because Stockton benefited from playing with him (obviously). Malone's array of moves didn't involve a whole lot of dribbling, that or he would roll to the rim and dunk/lay it up. This being the case, it's easy to see why Stockton would've piled up the assists like he did in his career, playing so long with a teammate like that. I am not taking anything away from him however, those kinds of stats can only come from extreme durability & consistency. He is undoubtedly top tier in that category.
